scientific_findings: S05 correctly distinguishes adjusted Model1 from crude OR and the Table2, Table3 and supplemental adjustment specifications.
S05 identifies E1 as raw-laboratory history and E2 as the CDC-harmonized revision, preserves author-code uncertainty, and separates dietary-weight candidate B from the primary A denominator.

S05 describes inferred supplemental populations and explicitly reports their distinct denominators and eleven unknown diagnosed/treated statuses rather than treating the cases as an exhaustive partition.
S05 interprets subgroup differences using joint Wald tests rather than comparing significance labels; it retains confounding, reverse-causation, measurement and missing-indicator limitations.

S06 distinguishes independent-binomial pointwise null rejection rates from conditional fixed-margin Fisher behavior and from the full null-space supremum size. Exact enumeration and Monte Carlo Wilson uncertainty are correctly separated.

S06 separates crude OR and prevalence ratio, expresses the 7.40% discrepancy as a relative difference in numerical ratios rather than a disease-risk increase, and prohibits converting adjusted OR to RR.
S06 labels McNemar as an educational synthetic paired example and marks actual NHANES application not applicable; it preserves the warning-collection limitation.

S07 reports partial reconstruction rather than exact author-code reproduction, acknowledges publication-value exposure without a blinding claim, and limits conclusions to association and statistical structure.
The notes distinguish numerical/data review acceptance from identification of the authors' hidden analytic choices and are consistent with the accepted V1, R2 and E2 scope.
nonblocking_precision_notes: The phrase survey t degrees of freedom is valid but model residual degrees of freedom would be more specific for the forest caption. The linked formula/df records already provide the exact convention.

The shared-denominator sentence describes the upstream primary cohort; subsequent B and supplemental paragraphs correctly state their separate denominators. Shared reference cohort would be a less ambiguous phrase if the text is edited later.
